Protein Design by Directed Evolution Guided by Large Language Models (IEEE TEVC, 2025)
Industrial wastewater contains dyes, plastics, phenolic compounds, oils, and other persistent pollutants.
Many natural enzymes lose activity under extreme pH and temperature conditions.
AI-assisted enzyme recommendation and optimization pipeline
Initial study focuses on PET plastic, phenolic compounds, textile dyes, and oil-containing wastewater because public enzyme datasets are available for these categories.

To develop an AI-assisted platform that recommends and computationally evaluates enzyme variants suitable for industrial wastewater under specified environmental conditions such as pH and temperature.
Identify pollutant-specific enzyme families from public biological databases.
Collect sequence, structure, and enzyme-property datasets.
Build a condition-aware computational pipeline using Protein Language Models.
Predict enzyme fitness and stability in-silico.
Wild-type/natural enzymes degrade only a narrow range of industrial pollutants and fail under extreme pH/temperature conditions – disadvantage.
Manual wet-lab directed evolution (mutagenesis + screening) is slow, costly, and combinatorially intractable.
Computational screening is used to reduce the number of enzyme variants that need laboratory testing.
In-silico, condition-aware mutation screening can shortlist promising enzyme variants before wet-lab testing, saving time and cost
Eliminates the need to exhaustively screen the mutation space experimentally for every new waste stream
